parts.article:
Report on a university drama project
 
Drama student Imogen Clare-Wood describes a collaborative theatre project she took part in
 
(A) This project was born from discussions I had with other drama students about the kind of theatre productions we’d like to create. Although we had previously been involved in various university productions where we took on specific roles, such as costume designer, producer, director and so on, we now wanted to take a collaborative approach that was new to all of us. We wanted a project in which every voice would carry equal weight and everyone would be able to contribute to every aspect of the show. We decided that the way to achieve this feeling of collaboration would be to concentrate on the process by which the work emerged during auditions and rehearsals. We chose a play that we felt allowed varied interpretations – Harold Pinter’s The Lover, a modern one-act play with just two characters. We decided we would use six actors cast as three different couples, and each pair would have a turn to perform on one of the three nights that the play was to be staged.
 
(B) The next step was to hold auditions in order to find six actors who felt the same way about the project as we did. We were anxious not to create an “us-and-them” feeling to the auditions, since collective ownership of the project was crucial to our ideas. So we ran the first round of auditions as a series of workshops, which we kept very informal and relaxed. Then we recalled fifteen actors for the second round of auditions. At this stage we wanted the reactions and ideas to flow and be explored by the group in the form of a discussion. We were looking for actors who could encourage other people’s ideas but who were also eager to input their own thoughts. Possibly the hardest part of the whole process was sitting down afterwards and deciding on the final six actors who would take part in the project.
 
(C) Our initial rehearsals were dedicated to creating a strong group dynamic and to exploring some of the themes of the play without explicit reference to the script. One of the strongest tools we used for this was freewriting – an exercise in which one person would read out a list of unconnected words and the rest of the group would clear their minds and simply write something in response to those words. We found it helped us to gain insight into the different ways our minds work. It also meant that we got to know each other very well, very quickly!
 
(D) It was only during the next phase of rehearsals that we finally began to work with the script. We had not yet decided on the pairings for the six actors at this point, and we had the non-actors on the team reading in addition to the people who would be doing the final performances. The whole team finally decided on the pairings of the actors by a vote, and, miraculously, it was a unanimous decision. The casting of the roles worked well and felt more natural than it had in any other show I’ve worked on. I think the dynamic that we developed over the early rehearsals was crucial in giving us three such strong onstage relationships.
 
(E) Other decisions were made in much the same way. The publicity was the responsibility of one member of the team, but she asked everyone what they thought would be effective. She then made several different versions, and from these we chose the design we liked the most. The stage set was left more to the individual pairs of actors, but since a large part of the later rehearsals was observing and feeding back on the individual performances being created by each pair, everyone was able to help with set design. We initially planned that each pair would use the same stage set. However, due to the different ways they interpreted the script, it became important for the set to be adapted for each couple.
 
(F) In the final performances, it was surprising that despite the collaborative nature of the project, a range of very different interpretations emerged. This is, of course, partly due to the tragicomic nature of Pinter’s text, which allowed the pairs of actors to exploit these two disparate elements, tragedy and comedy, to different degrees.
 
(G) The question-and-answer session held after the show was perhaps the most rewarding part of the project. The questions that the audience asked were interesting and insightful, and certainly made everyone in the team think about what we’d been doing, what we’d wanted to achieve and whether we’d achieved it. We were asked, among other things, about how successful our collaborative ethic had been, how we’d ended up with three such different shows, how we’d overcome the initial “production-team-versus-cast” divide, and how we would continue in the future.

reference:
Q1

干扰 注意题目要求填一个词，不要自己脑补填成“performance”或“rehearsals”，严格按照原文的“concentrate on the process”对应“focusing on the process”。

句子 第一段："We decided that the way to achieve this feeling of collaboration would be to concentrate on the process by which the work emerged during auditions and rehearsals."

解析 题目问一开始希望协作项目把重点放在制作戏剧的什么上，原文明确说是把重点放在试镜和排练中形成作品的“过程（process）”上。

Q2

解析 题目问第二轮试镜是以什么形式组织的，原文直接说以“讨论（discussion）”的形式来探索想法。

干扰 题目要求填名词单数，原文是“in the form of a discussion”，直接照抄“discussion”即可，不要填成第一轮的形式“workshops”。

句子 第二段："Then we recalled fifteen actors for the second round of auditions. At this stage we wanted the reactions and ideas to flow and be explored by the group in the form of a discussion."

Q3

解析 题目问在早期排练中发现了什么是一个有效的技巧，原文说使用的最有力工具（strongest tools/effective technique）是“自由写作（freewriting）”。

干扰 这题定位很直接，只需认识到原文的“strongest tools”就是题目里的“effective technique”，把专有名词“freewriting”抄对就好。

句子 第三段："Our initial rehearsals were dedicated to creating a strong group dynamic... One of the strongest tools we used for this was freewriting - an exercise in which one person would read out a list of unconnected words and the rest of the group would clear their minds and simply write something in response..."

Q4

干扰 题目中的“later rehearsals”对应原文的“next phase of rehearsals”，抓住这个时间状语的替换就能锁定“script”。

解析 题目问什么东西只在后期的排练中才使用，原文说直到排练的下一阶段，我们才终于开始使用“剧本（script）”。

句子 第四段："It was only during the next phase of rehearsals that we finally began to work with the script."

Q5

解析 题目问每个人都拥有一项什么来决定角色由谁来演，原文说整个团队最终通过一次“投票（vote）”决定了演员的配对。

干扰 题目有冠词“a”，原文也是“by a vote”，只要不填成“decision”这个结果名词就不会错。

句子 第四段："The whole team finally decided on the pairings of the actors by a vote, and, miraculously, it was a unanimous decision."

Q6

解析 题目问各种各样什么的出现令人惊讶，原文直接说出现了一系列非常不同的“诠释/演绎（interpretations）”让人吃惊。

干扰 题目“the variety of”对应原文“a range of very different”，空格必须填复数形式的“interpretations”，千万别漏了“s”。

句子 第六段："In the final performances, it was surprising that despite the collaborative nature of the project, a range of very different interpretations emerged."

Q7

句子 第一段："Although we had previously been involved in various university productions where we took on specific roles, such as costume designer, producer, director and so on, we now wanted to take a collaborative approach that was new to all of us."

干扰 你可能只看到前半句“previously been involved in various university productions”就选了TRUE，但必须看清前半句说的是承担“特定角色（specific roles）”而非协作。

解析 原文明确说这种协作方式（collaborative approach）对所有人来说都是“全新的（new to all of us）”，这与题干说作者以前参与过协作式制作完全相反。

Q8

解析 原文清楚说明每一对演员轮流在三个晚上的“其中一个晚上（one of the three nights）”演出，而不是像题干说的一个演员连演三晚。

干扰 搞清楚分配逻辑，一共演三晚，共有三对演员，刚好一对演一晚，不要把“one of the three nights”看成“for three nights”。

句子 第一段："We decided we would use six actors cast as three different couples, and each pair would have a turn to perform on one of the three nights that the play was to be staged."

Q9

解析 文中虽然提到了早期的排练（initial rehearsals）内容，但自始至终都没有提及这些排练具体的地点是不是在“大学剧院（university theatre）”。

干扰 不要因为文章标题有“university drama project”就理所当然地认为排练一定在大学剧院，脑补的地点信息一律选 NOT GIVEN。

句子 第三段："Our initial rehearsals were dedicated to creating a strong group dynamic and to exploring some of the themes of the play without explicit reference to the script."

Q10

句子 第四段："The whole team finally decided on the pairings of the actors by a vote, and, miraculously, it was a unanimous decision. The casting of the roles worked well and felt more natural than it had in any other show I've worked on."

解析 原文说作者觉得这次角色选派效果很好（worked well），而且比她参与过的任何演出都感觉“更自然（more natural）”，说明她对搭档配对非常满意。

干扰 原文中的“worked well”和“more natural”就是对题干中“felt satisfied”的完美情感替换，不要怀疑这种正向评价。

Q11

解析 原文只说了每个人都能帮忙进行布景设计（help with set design），但完全没有提及任何人发现了“意想不到的天赋（unexpected talent）”。

干扰 “能帮忙”不等于“有天赋”，更不等于“意外发现的天赋”，不要对简单的事实陈述进行过度夸张的推理。

句子 第五段："The stage set was left more to the individual pairs of actors, but since a large part of the later rehearsals was observing and feeding back on the individual performances being created by each pair, everyone was able to help with set design."

Q12

解析 原文明确说他们最初计划（initially planned）每对演员使用“相同的（same）”舞台布景，这跟题干说的最初打算使用“不同的（different）”布景完全相反。

干扰 题干说的是“original intention”（最初的意图），千万别因为看到原文后面说了“后来因剧本诠释不同而改变了布景（adapted for each couple）”就觉得题干是对的。

句子 第五段："We initially planned that each pair would use the same stage set. However, due to the different ways they interpreted the script, it became important for the set to be adapted for each couple."

Q13

解析 原文清楚地写明问答环节让团队每个人都在思考他们“想要实现什么（what we'd wanted to achieve）”，这完全等同于题干中的“思考他们的目标（think about their aims）”。

干扰 这题属于词汇同义替换，"aims"（目标）直接替换了 "what we'd wanted to achieve"（我们想要实现的事），非常直接对应。

句子 第七段："The questions that the audience asked were interesting and insightful, and certainly made everyone in the team think about what we'd been doing, what we'd wanted to achieve and whether we'd achieved it."
